programme.title: Beyond Paradise
programme.desc: Festive instalment of the detective drama. Humphrey has his hands full with a flurry of seasonal cases, while Martha is busy with a task of her own. Enlisting the help of Anne, Zoe and a special guest she races to pull off a secret plan. With an influx of unexpected visitors, a slew of holiday crimes to crack and a heartwarming reunion on the line, the team struggles to juggle it all and still be ready for a life-changing reveal. Starring Kris Marshall and Sally Bretton, with guest appearances by Adrian Edmondson, James Lance and Jonny Weldon.(n)

programme.title: Amanda & Alan's Spanish Job
programme.desc: In the sun-kissed hills of Andalusia, Amanda Holden and Alan Carr continue their work on renovating a run-down townhouse, while also savouring the festive traditions of the region. The pair dance and sing at a Christmas lights switch-on in Malaga, enjoy the local culture and celebrate with residents. However, the duo discover they have very different ideas when it comes to Christmas decorations.(n)

programme.title: Celebrity MasterChef
programme.desc: Reality TV star GK Barry, actor Kola Bokinni, BBC disability correspondent Nikki Fox and comedian Iain Stirling show off their cooking skills in an effort to impress judges Grace Dent and John Torode. First, they must follow a recipe for a celebratory Christmas centrepiece - and with each dish having an Italian twist, the judges call in 2024 Celebrity MasterChef champion Vito Coppola to help judge the results. After that, the contestants have one simple task - serve up their ultimate Christmas dinner.(n)

programme.title: This Is BBC Two
programme.desc: Preview of upcoming programmes from BBC Two.(n)

programme.title: My Life at Christmas with Anita Rani
programme.desc: Children's TV presenter, child rights advocate and peer Floella Benjamin reveals what makes Christmas special for her, in this in-depth conversation, explaining how the season has been a marker for memorable moments in her career, family life and faith.(n)

programme.title: Royal Institution Christmas Lectures
programme.desc: Dr Chris van Tulleken presents the first of three lectures revealing what happens inside the human body when people eat . He begins with the journey that food takes through the human body and is joined by leading experts, including his twin brother Dr Xand, who uses an endoscope inside his own body. Plus, Prue Leith drops by with some confusing Christmas foods to help Chris crack the mysterious science of taste.(n)

programme.title: A Christmas Choir with Michelle McManus
programme.desc: The singer is joined at Glasgow's Kelvingrove Art Gallery by Rock Choir and Jordanhill School Choir to celebrate the festive season with classic and contemporary Christmas songs.(New).(n)

programme.title: Carols from King's
programme.desc: A celebration of Christmas from the candlelit Chapel of King's College, Cambridge. Led by the Dean, the Rev Dr Stephen Cherry. Music includes Philip Ledger's setting of On Christmas Night, Anton Bruckner's Ave Maria, and The Lamb by John Tavener. The story of the Nativity is read by members of King's College in the words of the King James Bible and in Christmas poems by Alfred, Lord Tennyson, UA Fanthorpe and Howard Thurman.(n)

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: A Matter of Loaf and Death
programme.desc: The duo open their own bakery, Top Bun, and business is soon booming - not least because a 'cereal killer' is targeting all the rival bakers in town. Even better, Wallace has caught the eye of local beauty Piella Bakewell, but Gromit is more concerned that his master might be the killer's next victim.(n)

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: A Grand Day Out
programme.desc: Nick Park's Bafta-winning film which introduced the animated inventor and his faithful canine sidekick to the world. Wallace is distraught when his cheese supply runs out, so he decides to take a trip to the moon. All he needs to do is build himself a space rocket. With the voice of Peter Sallis.(n)

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: Celia Imrie narrates a look at how the crime writer's murder mysteries have been treated by movie-makers over the years using a selection of BBC interviews and archive material.(n)

programme.title: The Nutcracker from the Royal Ballet
programme.desc: Performance of Peter Wright's Christmas-set ballet set to Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky's music, filmed at Covent Garden's Royal Opera House in 2023. The magician Herr Drosselmeyer is on a quest to save his nephew, who has been transformed into a Nutcracker doll by the wicked Queen of the Mice. The only way to break the spell is for the Nutcracker to find a girl to love.(New).(n)

programme.title: White Christmas
programme.desc: A pair of former soldiers start a new career as nightclub entertainers. They try to boost the popularity of their old commanding officer's struggling winter resort in Vermont by staging a series of extravagant shows, with a little help from their former army buddies and a talented singing sister act. Musical, starring Bing Crosby, Danny Kaye, Vera-Ellen, Dean Jagger, Sig Rumann, Mary Wickes, Anne Whitfield and Rosemary Clooney, featuring seasonal songs by Irving Berlin.(n)

programme.title: The King
programme.desc: His Majesty Charles III delivers his annual Christmas message to the nation and the Commonwealth.(New).(n)

programme.title: Evil Under the Sun
programme.desc: Hercule Poirot braves the heat and sand to investigate the murder of a glamorous stage star on an idyllic Adriatic holiday island. It becomes clear many people had reason to want the temperamental actress dead and the Belgian sleuth is soon hard at work figuring out which of her enemies eventually managed to kill her. Mystery, starring Peter Ustinov, Diana Rigg, James Mason, Maggie Smith and Jane Birkin.(n)

programme.title: Dad's Army at the BBC
programme.desc: Toby Jones, who played Captain Mainwaring in 2016's Dad's Army film, shares a selection of classic clips that feature Britain's favourite Home Guard platoon in appearances that took them beyond the confines of Walmington-on-Sea. Featuring Mainwaring dancing, sparring with Morecambe and Wise and the whole cast defending Buckingham Palace at the 1970 Royal Gala.(n)

programme.title: Dad's Army
programme.desc: Frazer is unable to hide his delight when Captain Mainwaring's disreputable brother gatecrashes a sherry party for local dignitaries and tries to reclaim a pocket watch his father promised him. Comedy first aired in 1975, starring Arthur Lowe in a dual role, with John Le Mesurier and John Laurie.(n)

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Hyacinth decides to build a dream kitchen in time for Christmas - but a series of unforeseen setbacks, culminating in Richard contracting an embarrassing fungal infection, reduces her plans to a farce. Meanwhile, Rose and Daisy make an alarming discovery in their father's room. Festive special from 1994, starring Patricia Routledge and Clive Swift.(n)

programme.title: The Morecambe and Wise Show: The Lost Tapes
programme.desc: The first of two rarely seen episodes from 1968, thought to be lost until they were found by an archive preservation expert in an abandoned cinema in Sierra Leone, West Africa. In this episode, Chris Langford sings an old favourite, Old Devil Moon, and Michael Aspel guest stars.(n)

programme.title: The Morecambe and Wise Christmas Show
programme.desc: Seasonal special first shown in 1975, in which the duo have a memorable meeting with Robin Day, join Pan's People and persuade Diana Rigg to join them in a play 'wot Ernie wrote'. Plus, the classic streaker sketch and Eric's encounter with his arch-enemy Des O'Connor.(n)

programme.title: Jaws
programme.desc: A New England seaside town's tourist season is turned into a nightmare by a giant killer shark. The local police chief's efforts to protect the public are thwarted by the greedy mayor, forcing him to join forces with a grizzled fisherman and an enthusiastic marine biologist to hunt and kill the monster predator. Steven Spielberg's blockbusting thriller, starring Roy Scheider, Richard Dreyfuss and Robert Shaw, with an Oscar-winning score by John Williams. The film also won Academy Awards for Best Sound and Best Film Editing.(n)

programme.title: Jaws @ 50: The Definitive Inside Story
programme.desc: Steven Spielberg shares his exclusive story behind the making of Jaws. From the novel to the film, it shocked readers and audiences and continues to influence pop culture decades later. With contributions from film-makers including Jordan Peele, James Cameron and Guillermo del Toro.(New).(n)

programme.title: And Now for Something Completely Different
programme.desc: The Monty Python members appear in their first movie, comprising re-enacted sketches from the first two series of the surreal comedy show. Highlights include the dead parrot sketch, the Lumberjack Song and the Upper-class Twit of the Year Race. Starring the usual team of John Cleese, Michael Palin, Graham Chapman, Eric Idle, Terry Jones and Terry Gilliam, with regular female sidekick Carol Cleveland.(n)

programme.title: Call the Midwife
programme.desc: The Poplar midwives and medics return for the first of a two-part festive special ahead of a new series next year. Fred and Violet fly out to Hong Kong to visit Derek - only to notice a large building has collapsed. Back in London, news of the disaster reaches Nonnatus house and an emergency rescue mission to Kowloon is hastily launched. But Derek warns the medics to take care, as the densely populated city is home to Triad gangs operating in the area.(n)

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman make one last Strictly appearance for the annual festive show, which sees celebrities Scarlett Moffatt, Melanie Blatt, Brian McFadden, Babatunde Aléshé, Nicholas Bailey and Jodie Ounsley - aka Gladiator Fury - entering the ballroom for a one-off turn around the floor. There's also a performance by boy band Blue, the professionals show the amateurs how it's done with a couple of yuletide routines and judges Shirley Ballas, Craig Revel Horwood, Motsi Mabuse and Anton Du Beke give their thoughts on the dances.(n)

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Bob Mortimer, Paul Whitehouse and terrier Ted head to Devon and Cornwall, arriving on a steam train. They fish the rivers Lyd and Camel in Devon and head out to sea in Cornwall on a traditional fishing boat. The pair are joined by local star Dawn French, their favourite doctor Anand Patel and visit chef Paul Ainsworth in his Padstow restaurant to prepare a Christmas feast of turbot.(n)

programme.title: This Is BBC Two
programme.desc: Preview of upcoming programmes from BBC Two.(n)

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Mathew Baynton, Mel Giedroyc, Harriet Kemsley and Charles Venn test their general knowledge skills in a variety of trivia-based games for a special festive show.(n)

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: New host Sophie Willan presents this festive special, inviting Strictly judge Anton Du Beke, comedian Lucy Beaumont, actress Susan Wokoma and Tom Wilson - better known to Gladiators fans as Hammer - to take part in a trio of sewing challenges. They must put their own twist on a pattern for a Santa present sack, turn second-hand party wear into outfits based on The Twelve Days of Christmas and create clothing for models inspired by their favourite seasonal treat. Judges Esme Young and Patrick Grant keep a close eye on every stitch and hem and decide which famous face deserves the festive title.(n)

programme.title: The Scarecrows' Wedding
programme.desc: Adaptation of the children's book by Julia Donaldson and Axel Scheffler, starring Rob Brydon, Jessie Buckley and Domhnall Gleeson. Two devoted scarecrows, Betty O'Barley and Harry O'Hay, plan a wedding to remember but, when Harry insists on leaving the farm to collect one last thing for their big day, a smooth-talking scarecrow named Reginald Rake swoops in with plans of his own. Chaos ensues, and soon Betty's in danger and everything is at risk - can Harry get back in time and save the day?(n)

programme.title: Best of Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek Brockway revisits three favourite walks from south-west Wales. On his first wander from Little Haven to Solva, he tries surfing, learns about a UFO sighting that stunned the world and helps a local artist create a mural. On his second creative close encounter, Derek discovers the place that captivated and inspired poet Dylan Thomas, as he takes a walk through the town of Laugharne on the Carmarthenshire coast. For his final flashback, Derek is back in Pembrokeshire, peek ing at seal pups, learning how to train a sheepdog and creating a unique giant sand circle.(n)

programme.title: Bringing Up Baby
programme.desc: A zany heiress tries to acquire the help of a timid palaeontologist in looking after her pet leopard. As she starts to fall for the bemused academic, she decides to stop him marrying his severe assistant, and accidentally endangers his efforts to get funding for his beloved museum. Screwball comedy, starring Cary Grant, Katharine Hepburn, May Robson, Charlie Ruggles and Barry Fitzgerald.(n)

programme.title: What's Up, Doc?
programme.desc: A timid professor in San Francisco for a conference bumps into an eccentric, disaster-prone woman whose antics throw his carefully ordered life into upheaval - while a case of mistaken identity involving a jewel thief and a government whistle-blower only adds to his woes. Comedy, starring Barbra Streisand, Ryan O'Neal and Madeline Kahn.(n)

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin Roberts heads to Cannock in Staffordshire to see a three-bed bungalow with a bizarre layout and also visits Alsager in Cheshire to see a three-bed semi with lots of space - it's just in all the wrong places. Martel Maxwell is in Hartlepool, Co Durham, to look round two-bed terrace in need of modernisation.(n)

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Charlie Ross presents the show from Ardingly in West Sussex, with experts Caroline Hawley and Tim Weeks on hand to help those competing to make the most profits by buying items with the intention of taking them to auction. Charlie also brings along a mysterious gadget, but can the locals guess what it might be?(n)

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Briony May Williams is on her home turf in Somerset as she helps a couple with a budget of £500,000 who are looking to swap their narrowboat for a more traditional house on dry land. She also visits a market garden initiative that operates alongside a hostel for the homeless and rural rough sleepers.(n)

programme.title: The Italian Job
programme.desc: A crook assembles a motley gang to steal £4million in gold bullion from an Italian armoured car, which brings Turin to a standstill and enables the robbers to make a quick getaway in a fleet of Minis - but they end up falling foul of the Mafia along the way. Crime comedy, starring Michael Caine, Noel Coward, Benny Hill, Tony Beckley and John Le Mesurier.(n)

programme.title: The Great Escape
programme.desc: The most rebellious Allied prisoners of war are sent to a supposedly escape-proof maximum-security detention camp during the Second World War. They plan an ingenious mass breakout by digging a tunnel, but even when free of the camp, making it across occupied Europe proves a dangerous journey. Drama, starring Steve McQueen, James Coburn, Donald Pleasence, James Garner, Charles Bronson and Richard Attenborough.(n)

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Mathew Baynton, Mel Giedroyc, Harriet Kemsley and Charles Venn test their general knowledge skills in a variety of trivia-based games for a special festive show.(New).(n)

programme.title: Celebrity Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie invites TV presenter Will Best, comedian Laura Smyth, Strictly professional Nikita Kuzmin and actress Jayne Wisener to answer questions on the actor Danny Dyer, the films of Baz Luhrmann, Cristiano Ronaldo and the Belfast punk pioneer Terri Hooley.(New).(n)

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Two 'sporting' teams, from previous series, the Wrestlers and Arrowheads, return to fight it out in another special edition of the quiz. Impressively, it only takes two clues for them to work out what connects 'Boxers' and 'Mayors of High Wycombe'. Hosted by Victoria Coren Mitchell.(n)

programme.title: Christmas University Challenge
programme.desc: The first ever Christmas series champions, from Trinity College, Cambridge, return to take on the Bristol team from series eight. Amol Rajan asks the questions.(New).(n)

programme.title: The Great Escaper
programme.desc: Former Royal Navy officer Bernie Jordan is happily settled with wife Rene at a care home. Unfortunately, he hasn't secured a place on the official British Royal Legion trip to France to the commemorate the 70th anniversary of the D-Day landings. Bernie needs to make the trip to Normandy for personal reasons, and with Rene's blessing, he sneaks off to pay his respects. Drama, starring Michael Caine and Glenda Jackson in her final film.(n)

programme.title: Jaws 2
programme.desc: The seaside resort of Amity is terrorised once again by a man-eating great white shark. While police chief Brody struggles to alert the townsfolk to the magnitude of the danger, a group of teenagers - including Brody's two sons - is adrift at sea in waters hunted by the shark. Director Jeannot Szwarc's thriller sequel, starring Roy Scheider, Lorraine Gary and Murray Hamilton, with John Williams once more providing the acclaimed score.(n)

programme.title: Blue Velvet
programme.desc: A college student discovers a severed ear in a field, and is drawn into the dangerous underworld of his apparently peaceful home town. As events unfold, his curiosity leads him to the sinister relationship between a violent sociopath and a beautiful singer, whose vulnerability and sexuality bewitch him. David Lynch's thriller, starring Kyle MacLachlan, Dennis Hopper, Isabella Rossellini and Dean Stockwell.(n)

programme.title: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse
programme.desc: Teenager Miles Morales is reunited with Gwen Stacy and encounters a team of Spider-People charged with protecting the multiverse. The emergence of a deadly new threat divides opinion on the best course of action and Miles finds himself pitted against former allies. Animated adventure, featuring the voices of Shameik Moore and Hailee Steinfeld.(n)

programme.title: This Is BBC Two
programme.desc: Preview of upcoming programmes from BBC Two.(n)

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Mojo and Bo need to move a crashed meteor, but every time Mojo goes near the big rock he can't stop dancing.(n)

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Cosima and Big Lizard camp out with a little crab.(n)

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: When Hoofius plays his grandfaun's old magical panpipes, his friends do exactly what he asks them to do.(n)

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: The Lemmings try to destroy the statues of Grizzy, but he will not let them ruin his art.(n)

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: The gang finds a container full of Yummy.(n)

programme.title: Stage Stars
programme.desc: Senior dancer Jakob hopes to compete in a prestigious ballet competition, but suffers an injury that could shatter his dreams. Meanwhile, the pressure is on for the Anything Goes cast, as rehearsals are hotting up and showtime is fast approaching - but there is always time for a classroom takeover!(n)

programme.title: Bro's in Control
programme.desc: Adam and Joe pretend to be robots, with one having to serve baked potatoes, and the other getting to work in an ice-cream shop.(n)

programme.title: Cooking Buddies
programme.desc: Buddy and Conker invite Aiyla to make spicy tomato pasta and learn the basics of karate.(n)

programme.title: Danger Mouse
programme.desc: A double-length musical special. Danger Mouse reluctantly takes part in Pink Dawn's re-enactment of Melted, a famous ice-themed musical phenomenon.(n)

programme.title: Boy Girl Dog Cat Mouse Cheese
programme.desc: The siblings try to prepare an awesome Christmas surprise for their parents, but things go wrong every step of the way.(n)

programme.title: Deadly Predators
programme.desc: Steve looks back at his top Deadly Predators from the series and meets the ultimate predator. He reviews the biggest and best stunts from the series and reveals how the team bought a giant air vortex cannon to the Deadly junkyard to demonstrate the predatory prowess of the sperm whale.(n)

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Lynn and Sandra in the Highlands get a surprise when they harvest their first batch of honey. The Rodgers family gather to give bull Mario a good send-off, while Raymond and Johnny discover their sheep are under threat from flystrike, and the only way to protect them is to put the entire flock of 1,600 through the sheepdip.(n)

programme.title: Double Indemnity
programme.desc: An insurance salesman has an affair with the wife of a client, who persuades him to help kill her husband for the policy he has arranged. While the plan is successful, one of the salesman's colleagues suspects foul play. Billy Wilder's thriller, starring Barbara Stanwyck, Fred MacMurray and Edward G Robinson. Co-scripted by Raymond Chandler from the novel by James M Cain.(n)

programme.title: Inside the Factory
programme.desc: Paddy McGuinness and Cherry Healey visit the Original Biscuit Bakers factory in Market Drayton, Shropshire, to learn how they produce 100,000 gingerbread biscuits each week. Historian Ruth Goodman joins astronaut Helen Sharman to explore Christmas in space and Bobby Seagull teaches Cherry how to wrap presents using maths.(n)

programme.title: The Seven Year Itch
programme.desc: A bored publisher revels in his new-found freedom after his wife and son go away to the country. When a beautiful but naive actress moves in upstairs, he is tempted to turn his fantasies of an affair with her into reality. But even in his dreams, his conscience has a way of tripping him up. Billy Wilder's comedy, starring Marilyn Monroe, Tom Ewell, Evelyn Keyes and Oscar Homolka.(n)

programme.title: Some Like It Hot
programme.desc: After witnessing a Mob hit in Chicago, two male jazz musicians don drag and hide out with an all-girl band to evade the gangsters pursuing them. However, the pair struggle to disguise their attraction for the beautiful lead singer - while one of them catches the eye of a smitten millionaire. Billy Wilder's classic romantic comedy, starring Jack Lemmon, Tony Curtis and Marilyn Monroe.(n)

programme.title: Final Score
programme.desc: Jason Mohammad presents a round-up of the results and this afternoon's news from the Premier League, EFL and Scotland.(n)

programme.title: Dad's Army
programme.desc: The platoon challenges a rival regiment to a gruelling duel, involving map-reading, initiative tests, river-crossing and field-fighting, to prove they are fitter and better trained than any other troop. Christmas special of the comedy with the bumbling Home Guard of Walmington-on-Sea from 1971, starring Arthur Lowe, John Le Mesurier and Ian Lavender.(n)

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: In a festive episode first broadcast in 1995, Hyacinth resorts to alternative methods of recruitment when she gets no response to the adverts for a pageant she is directing. Suburban sitcom, starring Patricia Routledge.(n)

programme.title: Fawlty Towers
programme.desc: Basil's belief that guests are an obstacle to the smooth running of his hotel is borne out by the arrival of an aggressive woman (Joan Sanderson), and the tension between the two leads to a series of increasingly heated arguments. Classic comedy, starring John Cleese, Prunella Scales, Andrew Sachs and Connie Booth.(n)

programme.title: Lives Well Lived
programme.desc: Kirsty Wark looks back at the extraordinary lives of some of the acting greats, celebrated singers and political giants who died in 2025. Reese Witherspoon, Ralph Fiennes, Elizabeth McGovern and Bob Woodward are among those paying tribute to Robert Redford, Diane Keaton and Gene Hackman, while James Galway and Sheila Hancock honour their friend, jazz singer Dame Cleo Laine. Dominic Monaghan remembers both Patricia Routledge's dramatic and comic performances, while John Cusack, Sting and Al Jardine describe how Brian Wilson reinvented pop music in the 1960s.(New).(n)

programme.title: Unforgiven
programme.desc: Two notorious gunslingers come out of retirement to help a young assassin collect the $1,000 bounty on the heads of a pair of cowboys who attacked and mutilated a prostitute in the backwoods town of Big Whiskey. The local sheriff, however, has no intention of letting the pair impinge on his own authority. Oscar-winning Western, directed by and starring Clint Eastwood, with Gene Hackman, Morgan Freeman, Jaimz Woolvett and Richard Harris.(n)

programme.title: Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid
programme.desc: Two notorious outlaws' routine of bank and train robberies is cut short when a seemingly unstoppable posse is formed to catch them. The pair plan to flee America and start a new life in Bolivia, with the Sundance Kid's schoolmistress lover in tow - but staying ahead of the law is not so easy. Western, starring Paul Newman, Robert Redford and Katharine Ross.(n)

programme.title: Cleo Laine at the BBC
programme.desc: A look back at the singer's finest moments on the BBC, shown to coincide with her 95th birthday. Britain's 'First Lady of Jazz' became a star after joining The John Dankworth Seven in the 1950s, later marrying the bandleader. Internationally renowned for her mastery of the scat singing style, Cleo has now enjoyed over six decades of success and acclaim here and across the world. Featuring renditions of Send in the Clowns and I Love You Porgy, and duets with John Williams, Dudley Moore, Tony Bennett and her late husband Johnny Dankworth.(n)

programme.title: The War Between the Land and the Sea
programme.desc: Barclay stands alone, UNIT is powerless and the oceans rise as the war reaches its climax. While traitors conspire, can Barclay find Salt before it is too late? Doctor Who spin-off about a conflict between the human race and an ancient species of aquatic reptiles. Starring Russell Tovey and Gugu Mbatha-Raw.(n)

programme.title: Call the Midwife
programme.desc: Conclusion of the two-part story. In Hong Kong, Sister Julienne and Sister Hilda face down Denzil, who demands the keys to the Order's new property. Trixie and Geoffrey walk Mr Fischer home and learn he has a terminal blood disorder, so they hastily arrange for a rabbi to visit for the first night of Chanukah, the Jewish feast of lights. Rosalind and Joyce host a Christmas gathering at Nonnatus House with their friends and medical colleagues, while Sister Catherine decides to find out what happened to Queenie's baby.(n)

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: The craft experts spread a little Christmas joy, visited by special guests including Helen Mirren, who brings along a dilapidated cello belonging to a care home for people who have worked in the entertainment industry. Also popping in are children's author Julia Donaldson and Rob Brydon, who are seeking a repair to a toy farmhouse given to Julia by her granny. The experts also repair a life-size mechanical Rudolph belonging to Leicestershire Fire Service, a broken 80-year-old sledge for a Northern Ireland family and a tattered carol book that has played a central role as part of a local tradition in Sheffield.(n)

programme.title: This Is BBC Two
programme.desc: Preview of upcoming programmes from BBC Two.(n)

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Mathew Baynton, Mel Giedroyc, Harriet Kemsley and Charles Venn test their general knowledge skills in a variety of trivia-based games for a special festive show.(n)

programme.title: Prayer and Reflection
programme.desc: A traditional Presbyterian Christmas service from St Giles' Cathedral, Edinburgh, with a combination of scripture, readings and a sermon led by the Rev Dr Scott Rennie. The congregation join in a selection of hymns and carols performed by St Giles' Choir with musical director Jack Oades.(n)

programme.title: Lives Well Lived
programme.desc: Kirsty Wark looks back at the extraordinary lives of some of the acting greats, celebrated singers and political giants who died in 2025. Reese Witherspoon, Ralph Fiennes, Elizabeth McGovern and Bob Woodward are among those paying tribute to Robert Redford, Diane Keaton and Gene Hackman, while James Galway and Sheila Hancock honour their friend, jazz singer Dame Cleo Laine. Dominic Monaghan remembers both Patricia Routledge's dramatic and comic performances, while John Cusack, Sting and Al Jardine describe how Brian Wilson reinvented pop music in the 1960s.(n)

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker, Anita Rani and Adam Henson uncover the magic of Cadgwith on the Cornish coast at Christmas. From tree deliveries to seasonal pasty-making and a pub full of sea shanties, they see how the community comes together at this special time of year - all building to the big switch-on that floods the cove with festive lights.(n)

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek Brockway heads for the hills and a seasonal tour of the best pathways in Wales. In this episode, he goes for a windy walk through the country's only geopark and heads deep into the woods to follow the footsteps of a warrior and wizard.(New).(n)

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie Vipond takes a winter walk in Glen Affric in the Highlands for a special festive edition looking back at highlights from the programme in 2024, revisiting stories that Anne Lundon, Arlene Stuart, Cammy Wilson, Rosie Morton and Shahbaz Majeed have covered. Dougie reflects on the big themes, the best places and the inspiring people the team have met while travelling thousands of miles across the Scottish countryside. Plus, the winner of the BBC Scotland Local Food Hero Award is revealed at the BBC Food and Farming Awards.(n)

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt presents party food ideas from Yotam Ottolenghi, Crystelle Pereira and Poppy O'Toole. while actress Emilia Fox faces either her food heaven or hell.(New).(n)

programme.title: Remarkable Places to Eat
programme.desc: Michel Roux Jr takes Fred Sirieix for a Christmas treat in his favourite British city, Bristol. First up is a French bistro where they enjoy a stunning cote de boeuf and Michel makes aligot, known as the best mashed potato in the world. The duo then enjoy a swim in one of Britain's oldest lidos, which has an award-winning restaurant serving up a delicious breakfast. Escaping to the countryside, they visit a hotel and restaurant where Fred makes buffalo mozzarella, while Michel samples the hotel's own cider, before a return to the city and the multicultural neighbourhood of St Paul's, where they learn to cook Caribbean jerk turkey.(n)

programme.title: Snow Wolf Family and Me
programme.desc: Part one of two. Wildlife cameraman Gordon Buchanan hopes to get closer to wild wolves than anyone before to discover the true nature of this feared predator and heads to the north of Canada in search of a pack that has never seen people and so has no fear of humans. He begins to gain the trust of an Arctic wolf family and as time passes becomes accepted by the pack, including a female and its three newborn pups, and has some close encounters that reveal a softer side to the animals.(n)

programme.title: Casablanca
programme.desc: The American expat owner of a Moroccan nightclub is reunited with his old flame during the Second World War. Now married to a Czech freedom fighter, she needs his help to get them safely out of the country before they are captured by the Nazis - but the former lovers also have to wrestle the temptation to rekindle their simmering romance. programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: The broadcaster continues his bug-eyed view of the world of creepy-crawlies, revealing how predators defuse the defences of their prey. Highlights include the cockroach wasp, busy preparing a tasty - and very live - treat for its young, the whirligig beetle, which employs a water-based radar system, and the jumping portia spider, which feeds on other arachnids.(n)

programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: A further selection of creepy-crawly close-ups, focusing on courtship in the bug world. Highlights include scorpions shaking their booty, the perfume-wearing nasonia wasp and the tropical cricket, for whom romance goes out of the window as it uses bribery to seal the deal with would-be partners. One potential partner to steer well clear of, however, is the praying mantis, the female of which is notorious for eating the male just after - or even during - mating. Narrated by David Attenborough.(n)

programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: A close-up view of sex, bug-style, as David Attenborough talks viewers through the different ways in which creepy-crawlies reproduce. Size matters for the minuscule male orb spider, creepily sneaking up on its intended and trying to mate without her noticing, while there's no rest for the lothario-like butterfly, which has plenty of notches on its proverbial bedpost. However, the harvestman spider has no use for sex at all, and reproduces by cloning itself.(n)

programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: David Attenborough shifts the focus to bugs that prefer co-operation rather than conflict. They include burrowing cockroaches, the suitably named social spiders - which share a 30-metre web - the queen bee and her happy hive of workers and green ants pulling together to build a nest.(n)

programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: The broadcaster concludes his close-up examination of the creepy-crawly world, shifting focus to the bugs' ultimate invention - the colony. Key residents of these minuscule mega-cities include honey bees, termites, leafcutter ants - who have a knack for farming - and their Argentine cousins, members of a community so vast it spans an entire continent.(n)

programme.title: David Attenborough's Dragons and Damsels
programme.desc: Arguably more beautiful than butterflies, better fliers than hummingbirds and with intriguing and complex behavioural patterns - dragonflies and damselflies are marvels of the insect kingdom. This documentary uses the latest camera technology to show their manoeuvres, mating strategies, territorial behaviour and flight dynamics, revealing them to be the ultimate insect.(n)

programme.title: David Attenborough's Rise of Animals
programme.sub-title: From the Seas to the Skies
programme.desc: Part one of two. The naturalist explores the evolution of vertebrates over the past 500 million years, beginning with a look at how remarkable advances allowed primitive fish to make the radical move on to land, and then take to the skies with the advent of flight. He uses fossils of both ancient and living species combined with CGI and film to chart their journey out of the water to populate all corners of the globe.(n)

programme.title: David Attenborough's Rise of Animals

programme.title: David Attenborough's Kingdom of Plants

programme.title: David Attenborough's Conquest of the Skies
programme.desc: The veteran naturalist examines the world of flight, travelling across the globe to chart the evolutionary story of those creatures who seemingly defy the rules of gravity by taking to the air. Initially focusing on insects, Attenborough meets a descendant of the dragonfly, before examining the Atlas beetle, which tends to restrict flight to times when it needs a mate or a fresh supply of food. More aesthetically pleasing is a group of beautiful tropical butterflies, followed by an in-depth study into the blow fly - the jet fighter of insects.(n)

programme.title: David Attenborough's Conquest of the Skies
programme.desc: The veteran naturalist visits the jungles of Borneo to meet creatures that like to glide through life - the harlequin tree frog and the little-known colugo - often referred to, incorrectly, as a flying lemur. He also has a CGI-assisted encounter with the first true vertebrate flyer, the pterosaur, receives a flying lesson from a small flock of swans at Loch Lomond in Scotland and encounters the planet's largest species of bat.(n)

programme.title: David Attenborough's Conquest of the Skies
programme.desc: The veteran naturalist turns his attention to creatures that dominate the skies today. He begins with the vast bird family, watching a group of vultures as they go scavenging and some peregrine falcons dive bombing for their prey. He then moves on to the floating forests of Ecuador to find out what makes the humble hummingbird tick, before ending his journey at the Gomantong bat caves of Borneo - a place he first filmed in 1972 - witnessing a mass exodus of the creatures.(n)

programme.title: Attenborough at 90: Behind the Lens
programme.desc: A profile of broadcaster and naturalist David Attenborough, whose career has included being the first controller of BBC Two and making numerous groundbreaking wildlife programmes.(n)

programme.title: Attenborough's Journey
programme.desc: Documentary following David Attenborough as he journeys around the world to make his series First Life, which explores the origins of life on Earth. As he visits locations including the Great Barrier Reef, the deserts of Morocco and the glaciers of Canada, the broadcaster and wildlife expert explains his life-long fascination with the natural world, and also travels back to Leicestershire, the county in which he spent his childhood.(n)

programme.title: David Attenborough Meets Obama
programme.desc: Another chance to see Barack Obama's conversation, recorded in May 2015, with renowned naturalist and film-maker David Attenborough. In a twist on usual convention, the then-US president took the role of interviewer, quizzing Attenborough about his thoughts on the future of the planet, their shared passion for nature, and potential ways to protect the environment. Also includes behind-the-scenes footage from Sir David's latest project on the Great Barrier Reef, as well as highlights from throughout the veteran broadcaster's career.(n)

programme.title: Great Barrier Reef with David Attenborough
programme.desc: Following his visit to the Great Barrier Reef in 1957, naturalist and broadcaster David Attenborough returns and uses the latest filming techniques to unlock the secrets of the natural wonder. In the first edition, he descends beneath the waves at night and uses cutting-edge technology to generate computer scans of the sea floor. He also learns about a complex community of animals, as well as the annual coral spawning, which is responsible for the great diversity in the reef.(n)

programme.title: Great Barrier Reef with David Attenborough
programme.desc: Using the latest technology, the naturalist explores the shark-infested waters of Osprey Reef in the Triton submersible, before returning to the nesting grounds of the Green Sea Turtle, 60 years after his first visit to Raine Island. He also marvels at manta ray cleaning stations on Lady Elliot Island, and tracks dwarf minke whales to discover their surprising reasons for returning, and why the reef is vital for their survival.(n)

programme.title: Great Barrier Reef with David Attenborough
programme.desc: The naturalist examines what the next few decades may hold for this remarkable ecosystem, and looks at the work of scientists who are trying to preserve the area and the species that inhabit it, assisted by research vessel the Alucia. He also embarks on an ambitious attempt to dive further into the reef than ever before to witness the resilient coral that live down in the depths and see if they hold answers that may help to overcome challenges that lie ahead, as the impact of humans on the reef continues to take its toll.(n)

programme.title: David Attenborough's First Life
programme.desc: In the first of a two-part documentary, the naturalist explores the origins of life on Earth. Beginning the journey near his childhood home in Charnwood Forest, Leicestershire, he learns how a fossil discovery transformed scientists' understanding of the evolution of complex organisms, and in Newfoundland and Australia he reveals the earliest kinds of animal to exist on the planet. With the help of cutting-edge technology and visual effects, the programme brings the creatures to life, demonstrating how they survived.(n)

programme.title: David Attenborough's First Life
programme.desc: In the conclusion of the two-part documentary, the naturalist travels to Burgess Shale in Canada's Rocky Mountains, where he explores how evolution gained pace once creatures developed mouths and mobility. In Scotland, he reveals that one of the smallest fossils found holds the secret to how animals began surviving on dry land, and explains the bloom of life during the oxygen-rich Carboniferous period.(n)

programme.title: The Bachelor King
programme.desc: Documentary exploring the lives of king penguins, filmed on the sub-Antarctic island of South Georgia over five months. The programme imagines what one penguin's life would be, following it during the challenging, awkward time between adolescence and adulthood. Presented by David Attenborough.(n)

programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: David Attenborough employs the latest technologies to explore the violence, rivalries and deadly weaponry existing within the world of bugs. This first episode examines the survival tactics of its terrifying residents including killer ants, trap-setting spiders and beetles with the ability to shoot boiling chemicals at their enemies.(n)

programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: The broadcaster continues his bug-eyed view of the world of creepy-crawlies, revealing how predators defuse the defences of their prey. Highlights include the cockroach wasp, busy preparing a tasty - and very live - treat for its young, the whirligig beetle, which employs a water-based radar system, and the jumping portia spider, which feeds on other arachnids.(n)

programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: A further selection of creepy-crawly close-ups, focusing on courtship in the bug world. Highlights include scorpions shaking their booty, the perfume-wearing nasonia wasp and the tropical cricket, for whom romance goes out of the window as it uses bribery to seal the deal with would-be partners. One potential partner to steer well clear of, however, is the praying mantis, the female of which is notorious for eating the male just after - or even during - mating. Narrated by David Attenborough.(n)

programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: A close-up view of sex, bug-style, as David Attenborough talks viewers through the different ways in which creepy-crawlies reproduce. Size matters for the minuscule male orb spider, creepily sneaking up on its intended and trying to mate without her noticing, while there's no rest for the lothario-like butterfly, which has plenty of notches on its proverbial bedpost. However, the harvestman spider has no use for sex at all, and reproduces by cloning itself.(n)

programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: David Attenborough shifts the focus to bugs that prefer co-operation rather than conflict. They include burrowing cockroaches, the suitably named social spiders - which share a 30-metre web - the queen bee and her happy hive of workers and green ants pulling together to build a nest.(n)

programme.title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
programme.desc: The broadcaster concludes his close-up examination of the creepy-crawly world, shifting focus to the bugs' ultimate invention - the colony. Key residents of these minuscule mega-cities include honey bees, termites, leafcutter ants - who have a knack for farming - and their Argentine cousins, members of a community so vast it spans an entire continent.(n)

programme.title: David Attenborough's Rise of Animals
programme.sub-title: From the Seas to the Skies
programme.desc: Part one of two. The naturalist explores the evolution of vertebrates over the past 500 million years, beginning with a look at how remarkable advances allowed primitive fish to make the radical move on to land, and then take to the skies with the advent of flight. He uses fossils of both ancient and living species combined with CGI and film to chart their journey out of the water to populate all corners of the globe.(n)

programme.title: David Attenborough's Galapagos
programme.desc: The broadcaster explores the Galapagos, a collection of volcanic islands in the Pacific known for its extraordinary wildlife. More than 150 years after Charles Darwin formulated his ground-breaking theory of evolution on the remote archipelago, Attenborough explains how life on the islands has continued to evolve in biological isolation, examining how the ever-changing volcanic landscape has given birth to species and sub-species that exist nowhere else in the world. He begins by revealing how Galapagos rose from the ocean four million years ago.(n)

programme.title: David Attenborough's Galapagos

David investigates the driving forces behind their evolution, exploring the appearance and behaviour of remarkable creatures and vegetation including giant whale sharks, marine iguanas and seemingly normal dandelion seeds that grow into plants the size of trees.(n)

programme.title: David Attenborough's Galapagos
